adoption_decisions.reason: ECC and gstack provide useful operator architecture, but ARTEMIS must keep its own source of truth, gates and artifacts.
Implementation must become original ARTEMIS contracts, scripts and validation artifacts.
Any future installable component must show file plan, permissions, rollback and validation before touching the project.
Hooks, browser automation, auth, provider runtime, token spend and remote writes remain Human Gate only.

rejected_paths.reason: Would blur authorship, licensing obligations, update surface and ARTEMIS authority.
Installers can mutate harness config, hooks and local state before ARTEMIS has preview and rollback gates.
ARTEMIS needs its own vocabulary, Socratic routing, Validation Gate and Human Gate boundaries.
Hooks can intercept commands and tool outputs; that is runtime enforcement and requires explicit approval.

operator_principles: External references are inspiration, not authority.
ARTEMIS owns the contract; Git, Exec Packs, Event Log and Validation Gate remain canonical.
No external code, prompt, asset, installer or hook is copied in this cut.
Every future operator capability must name provider fit, risk, validation and Human Gate conditions.
Learning and memory candidates must be governed before they can influence future work.
Security and browser/tool escape hatches are deny-default until explicitly allowed.
